title: Full review of release 0.2.74, with fixes: six findings, two of them security controls that did not control anything

AC1.note: Denominator stated and measured: 43 non-test source files, 36 test files, v0.2.73..v0.2.74. Six reviewers by area with distinct lenses — SAC integrity, harness process/lifecycle, flow+review wiring, CLI false-clean, skills registry, and the ten small scattered files that a large-diff-focused review stops reading. That last group produced the session-redaction finding.

AC2.note: Fourteen gates mutated. Non-vacuity established first by deleting the digest comparison, which returned 26 pass / 2 fail — a sweep that can only return green proves nothing. Result: 4 guarded by tests, 3 guarded by the compiler, 5 removable with the suite green, 1 multi-line throw not uniquely anchorable.

AC3.note: All six reviewers ran read-only and named mutation candidates instead of running them; mutations were executed centrally, one at a time. The reason is the defect this programme fixed in task-implementer: parallel agents sharing one worktree, where one destroys a wave-mate's uncommitted work it cannot observe.

AC4.note: Every finding carries a concrete failure scenario; reviewers dropped candidates that had none. Each also returned a checked-and-cleared list with reasons — which is how three fixes the release makes to OLDER leaks (memory, wiki, wiki-enrichment writing unredacted content despite computing a guard decision) were recorded rather than missed.

AC5.note: Two reviewers converged independently on the security-acknowledgement bypass from different directions (SAC and CLI), and the second added the decisive framing: pre-0.2.74 was a dead end where needs-approval could never be accepted, so the release traded permanently-broken for silently-defeated. I verified both security findings myself in the code before acting: the sole production minter, and the field-by-field redaction path.

AC6.note: Each of the ten fixes proved by restoring the exact shipped line and watching a named test go red 3/3 in isolation. Three of my own tests initially passed for the wrong reason and were caught by exactly this: one asserted printed output instead of the stored token, one sealed a checkpoint hash over the key it was testing, one omitted the session so the command failed identically with and without the guard. All three corrected, then re-proved.

AC7.note: The ignored-validator-keyword defect was fixed structurally rather than as a third instance: a guard asserting no shipped schema declares a keyword validateValue ignores, with the implemented set scraped from the validator source rather than hand-listed. It found two further real defects on its first run — exclusiveMinimum on a dispatch budget (zero and negative validated clean), and the "not" keyword, the only way a schema expresses a prohibition, which was decorative: the branch accepted exactly what it forbade.

AC8.note: The guard's first version reported $ref as unimplemented when it is implemented — the scrape pattern started at [a-zA-Z] and missed the leading dollar. Fixed before landing. A guard that cries wolf earns an allow-list entry and is then deleted, so the false positive was treated as the same class of error as a miss.

AC9.note: Named in PR #428 and here: two truncation lines remain individually removable because they are genuinely redundant — same refusal, same input — with a third check now backing both. The earlier flow-212 disposition claiming 'checked and cleared' for that pair is corrected: it rested on one being redundant without checking whether the other was pinned, and neither was. The hang is separately removed by bounding the loop.

AC10.note: typecheck clean; bun test 6399 pass / 18 skip / 0 fail against a 6386/0 baseline; test:guards 173/0; check:doc-links 1144 links / 0 broken; CI 12/12 on #427 and #428.
